claims.text: In a single-phase HEA containing at least five elements, Tc is primarily governed by effective valence electron concentration (VEC).
VEC modulates the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
VEC modulates electron-phonon coupling strength.
Increasing the proportion of heavy transition metals increases average VEC by adding more d electrons.
Higher average VEC enhances superconducting properties regardless of high mixing entropy.
Nb-Ti-Zr-Ta-Hf is an example of a five-element HEA relevant to the proposed comparison.
The example Nb-Ti-Zr-Ta-Hf alloy is a random, homogeneous, single-phase bcc or similar solid solution.
Composition can be varied to change VEC while keeping mixing entropy, phase purity, and crystal structure constant.
The homogeneous disordered arrangement ensures that VEC tuning consistently modifies the electronic band structure.
Changes in VEC alter d-electron occupancy at the Fermi level and thereby alter the density of states.
Changes in density of states influence electron-phonon coupling and can enhance or suppress Tc in a disordered HEA.
Samples with increased average VEC will show a systematic increase in Tc relative to a lower-VEC baseline.
Samples with increased average VEC may show an enhanced upper critical field relative to the baseline.
The predicted Tc increase will occur without significant changes in phase homogeneity.
The lower-VEC control alloy exhibits a lower Tc.
The proposed VEC relationship applies only while the alloy remains a moderately disordered, single-phase solid solution.
Sufficiently strong disorder can suppress superconductivity and invalidate the proposed trend.
Disorder-related quantum-critical behavior may cause deviations from a simple VEC-Tc trend.
Failure of higher-VEC samples to show a systematic Tc increase would falsify the primary-VEC hypothesis.
Failure of density of states and electron-phonon coupling to improve with VEC would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and prediction assert a directional increase of Tc with increasing VEC, whereas the mechanism only states that VEC changes can either enhance or suppress Tc and does not explain why the higher-VEC direction should increase Tc.

The design proposes varying elemental ratios while keeping mixing entropy fixed, but changing ratios generally changes configurational mixing entropy unless an explicit isoentropic substitution strategy is specified.
